answer: The relic detector writes to atlas, and grove makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 175 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 23 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 38 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
